ls_merge_basic.why: merge two patches by a joint-parity measurement; correct both patches on the outcome
ls_merge_basic.notes: Patches reduced to one data qubit each: the timing shape only.

ls_merge_eq.why: merge with an explicit EQ policy (arms padded equal)
ls_merge_eq.notes: Patches reduced to one data qubit each: the timing shape only.

ls_merge_slack.why: patch B is busy longer than patch A before the merge; a barrier restores the join (patch-sync slack)
ls_merge_slack.notes: The slack (400 ns) is paid by the barrier before the parity measurement. Patches reduced to one data qubit each: the timing shape only.

ls_merge_split_seq.why: merge, then split, in sequence under one policy
ls_merge_split_seq.notes: Patches reduced to one data qubit each: the timing shape only.

ls_merge_sync_delta.why: merge with an explicit sync(delta=100ns) policy
ls_merge_sync_delta.notes: Patches reduced to one data qubit each: the timing shape only.

ls_split_correction.why: split after a merge: two results, one correction per patch
ls_split_correction.notes: Reads c[1] right after its measurement: stale-read risk (O2a). Patches reduced to one data qubit each: the timing shape only.
